review_notes: I read the whole file and the `Diagram`/`Hom` definitions in IntervalBar.lean. I also checked Mathlib's `CommSq.vert_inv`/`horiz_inv`. Nothing was compiled, so the proposed lemma statements are sketches. In particular, the exact form of the `𝟙 _` factors after `change` depends on how `Diagram.map` and `wideSubcategoryInclusion` unfold. I did not read `Diagram.map`'s definition, and I did not check whether `RestrictedNerve.Strings` has a ready-made evaluation functor or iso-from-components lemma. I did not report the nine-line `reindexMonoidal` block or the `restricted_isIso`/`strings_isIso` pair, because the repeated parts there are short or routine.

findings.declaration: RestrictedNerve.stringVertexMap, transposeDiagramHom, untransposeDiagramObj, untransposeDiagramHom (unit/cut law normalisation)
findings.problem: Five proofs need the `Hom.unit` and `Hom.cut` laws of a morphism that has been pushed through `diagramInclusion`. Each time, the proof writes out a long `change` that spells the law with `𝟙 _ ≫ …` and `… ≫ 𝟙 _` factors. It then strips those factors with `erw [Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]`, and only afterwards applies the underlying law. This happens at lines 182-190 (`stringVertexMap`), 206-214 (`transposeDiagramHom`), 239-246 and 250-253 (unit, in `untransposeDiagramObj`), 269-273 and 278-282 (cut, in `untransposeDiagramObj`), and 315-332 (`untransposeDiagramHom`). The `change` statements are long and fragile, and each copy contains the same bookkeeping about the inclusion's identity factors.
findings.proposed_change: Prove two lemmas once, next to `diagramInclusion`. Each states the `Hom.unit` / `Hom.cut` law for `(diagramInclusion W I).map f` with the identity factors already removed. Their statements take the form `(F.app i i le_rfl) ≫ (B.unit i).hom = (A.unit i).hom` and `(F.app i j hij ⊗ₘ F.app j k hjk) ≫ (B.cut i j k hij hjk).hom = (A.cut i j k hij hjk).hom ≫ F.app i k _`. The cut statement is the `Hom.cut` field in IntervalBar.lean, with the inclusion's `𝟙 _` factors stripped. Each lemma is proved once by `change` followed by `simp`. Ideally the lemmas are phrased as `Hom` fields on the underlying morphism, so that `exact (f.hom.app t).hom.unit i` and `exact (F.obj.map f).hom.cut i j k hij hjk` close the goals. The five proofs then shrink to one-line applications. The `he`/`change`/`erw` blocks disappear, and the `erw` calls (which can be brittle) go with them.
findings.benefit: The definitions and proof-state massaging stay in one place. The two `Hom` laws now look the same wherever they are used. The long `change` statements, which are sensitive to how `Diagram.map` unfolds, are written once. Changing the representation of `diagramInclusion` later means fixing two lemmas instead of about ten proof blocks.

findings.declaration: RestrictedNerve.untransposeDiagramObj (inverse naturality of unit and cut)
findings.problem: For both `unit` and `cut`, the isomorphism is rebuilt in `Strings W n` from the componentwise isos `(F.obj.obj t).unit i` and `(F.obj.obj t).cut i j k …`. Only the naturality of `hom` is available, from `(F.obj.map f).hom.unit` and `.cut`. The naturality of `inv` is therefore re-derived by hand in each case. The `unit` version (lines 254-257) cancels a mono and the `cut` version (lines 283-290) cancels an epi. Both rewrite with `wide_inv_hom` / `wide_hom_inv`, `Category.assoc` and `he`. This is the same argument, 'the inverse of a commuting square of isos commutes', written twice. The two copies differ only in which side is cancelled, and the `cut` copy uses a fragile `repeat' erw [← Category.assoc]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one helper that builds an isomorphism in `Strings W n` from componentwise isos plus naturality of the forward components, and derives inverse naturality once. For example: `def Strings.isoOfComponents (e : ∀ t, U.obj.obj t ≅ V.obj.obj t) (nat : ∀ t s f, U.obj.map f ≫ (e s).hom.hom = (e t).hom.hom ≫ V.obj.map f) : U ≅ V`. It would be proved with `NatIso.ofComponents`, or from `CommSq.vert_inv` / `CommSq.horiz_inv` applied to the commuting square built from `nat`. Both `unit` and `cut` then supply only `nat`, which is the existing `he` after normalisation, and `hom_inv_id`/`inv_hom_id` come for free. The squares are over `WideSubcategory` morphisms. The helper therefore has to carry the `W`-membership proofs `f.property`, which is why a small `Strings`-specific lemma is needed instead of calling Mathlib directly.
findings.benefit: The inverse-naturality argument is written and checked once. The two blocks (about 45 lines) reduce to a naturality square each, and the `cancel_mono`/`cancel_epi` and `repeat' erw` manipulations leave the main definition.

findings.declaration: RestrictedNerve.stringVertex and untransposeDiagramObj (iso and axiom transport at a string vertex)
findings.excerpt: exact congrArg (fun f => f.hom.app t) (A.cut i j k hij hjk).inv_hom_id
findings.problem: `stringVertex` evaluates every isomorphism of `A` (`unit`, `cut`) at a vertex `t`. For each one it rebuilds the `hom`/`inv` pair, with the `W`-membership proof, and re-proves `hom_inv_id` and `inv_hom_id` by `congrArg (fun f => f.hom.app t)`. The blocks for `unit` (lines 149-157) and `cut` (lines 158-166) are identical apart from the iso being evaluated. The three coherence axioms (lines 167-175) repeat the same `hom_ext; congrArg …app t` pattern. `untransposeDiagramObj` does the converse at lines 259-306: it forgets the `W`-property componentwise, again with a copy per iso and per axiom. So the 'apply a `Strings`-iso at a vertex' reasoning is spread over about ten near-identical blocks.
findings.proposed_change: Define once an evaluation of an isomorphism in `Strings W n` at a vertex, `Strings.evalIso (e : U ≅ V) (t : Fin (n+1)) : (⟨U.obj.obj t⟩ : WideSubcategory W) ≅ ⟨V.obj.obj t⟩`. Its `hom` is `⟨e.hom.hom.app t, e.hom.property t⟩`, and its `hom_inv_id`/`inv_hom_id` come from `congrArg (fun f => f.hom.app t)`. Then `unit i := evalIso (A.unit i) t` and `cut i j k hij hjk := evalIso (A.cut i j k hij hjk) t`. The three axioms use the same lemma `evalIso_hom : (evalIso e t).hom.hom = e.hom.hom.app t` applied to `A.left_unit`, `A.right_unit` and `A.associativity`.
findings.benefit: This removes about 25 lines of copy-paste in `stringVertex`. The only mathematical fact used (evaluating a natural isomorphism at an object gives an isomorphism) is stated once. It also fits with the iso-from-components helper in the previous finding.
